result.title: What I tell my Stern Business School students on how to thrive in the age of AI
result.description:
For today's undergraduates, the impact of artificial intelligence on the jobs market means massive job uncertainty. So how should young people prepare themselves for the unknown unknowns of a career in the age of AI?

"The uncertainty will be overwhelming for a fraction of them, but I think for a fraction of them they will look back in 10 years and say this was a period of such great opportunity," says Arun Sundararajan, a professor of entrepreneurship, technology operations and statistics at New York University's Stern School of Business.

This episode was co-produced with China's CGTN and co-hosted by Xin Guan, CGTN anchor and chief business news editor.

result.title: This start-up turns discarded fishing nets into textiles
result.description:
Fishing nets can take decades to break down - and when they’re lost at sea, they can entangle marine life and damage ocean habitats.

Bureo collects discarded nets from around the world, then recycles them into nylon yarn for waterproof jackets, hats and sportswear.

Since 2013, the start-up has collected 7.7 million kilos of fishing nets - helping turn a major ocean problem into a source of new materials.

Bureo is supported by members of the 1000 Ocean Startups Coalition, which is committed to scaling at least 1,000 transformative solutions by 2030. Find out more: https://www.1000oceanstartups.org/about

result.title: Countries are scrambling to secure copper. Why?
result.description:
Why did Japan just lend $466 million to Chile’s state copper mining company?

The answer lies in the energy transition.

Whether it’s solar farms, data centres or electric vehicles, tomorrow’s infrastructure relies on critical minerals. And none is more crucial than copper, which is used almost anywhere electricity is generated, transmitted or used.

But with demand set to increase 40% by 2040 - and with the world on track to meet just 70% of that - nations are taking steps to shore up their #copper supplies for the future.

A World Economic Forum report maps the policy interventions that will be required to ensure there are enough critical minerals to meet demand: https://www.weforum.org/publications/making-critical-minerals-bankable-policy-tools-to-unlock-investment/

result.title: Meet the woman whose battery breakthrough could bring electricity to millions
result.description:
It was the forgotten idea of a Nobel-winning scientist. Now, Emilie Bodoin is turning it into reality.

The Founder and CEO of Pure Lithium has revived the ‘lithium metal battery’ – an alternative to the lithium-ion batteries we know from electric vehicles, and a breakthrough that could make batteries lighter, safer and more efficient – all while reducing dependence on critical mineral supply chains.

If successful, the technology could also help more countries manufacture batteries closer to home, strengthening energy security and supporting the transition to cleaner energy.

Pure Lithium is a World Economic Forum Technology Pioneer, part of a community of start-ups which are developing cutting-edge technologies with the potential to improve the world.
